Hello everyone,
My name is Michał, and for some time I've been invested in learning Lean and formal mathematics. My background is as a theoretical physicist, now turned software engineer. My biggest dream is to formalize physics - in fact PhysLib project is what brought me here.

For now I wanted to make some contributions to Mathlib, as I feel there are still a few things that I'd like to have when moving on to physics. I thought I could give a try bringing Gelfand Triple/Rigged Hilbert Spaces to mathlib (I REALLY like Dirac notation, and won't settle for projector-valued measures), and as a first step in that I wanted to implement the concept of nuclear spaces.

In that process I've proven some tiny lemmas which I found useful and I thought belong to already existing files. So, sticking to the motto "the smaller the better" from the contribution guide, I decided to wrap them in a few separate PRs, and make my first actual contribution.

The PR in question is #41731. I hope to get some feedback and comments, and help in getting it throught the submission - this is my first time contributing to any open source project.

Many thanks,
Michał

Hello again,
I have created another small PR #41827, which is a direct port of lifts from PiTensorProduct to binary TensorProduct. It allows for representing an element of a tensor product of two modules M and N the set of its lifts: all possible lists of pairs (m,n), where m ∈ M and n ∈ N, such that the sum of their tensor products m ⊗ n is the original element of M ⊗ N. It allows for forwards (lifts) and backwards (mem_lifts_iff) conversions, and establishes basic properties.

All the functions and properties are direct ports of their equivalents in the file Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/PiTensorProduct/Basic.html, so it should be quite easy to review. At the same time, this new API is needed to define the projective seminorm on the binary tensor product, which we need for defining nuclear operators, which is main main goal.

It's been sitting in the queue for quite some time now, and I begun to fear that merge conflicts will soon starts creeping in. I thought I'd mention it here and maybe someone would like to take a look.
It would help if you also PRed the rest for context though. You can make it into some draft PRs for example. Otherwise it's not immediately clear why they are needed

Thanks for the suggestion. Here is the PR in which I port the projective seminorm into the binary tensor product #41862, which directly depends on the PR from my previous post. The Nuclear Operator is still work in progress, but I'll post a draft as soon as it takes some proper shape.

I've also pursued a parallel path of defining the projective tensor product from the more abstract perspective, as the infimum of topologies #42127. This one I think is ready for review. The idea is to show that both topologies are the same (i.e. it is induced by the projective seminorm family). I think all the pieces are in place for that.
